title: Fourteen Winters and One Short Handle
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：drawer　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 drawer 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 my grandmother ① made a drawer that no child in the house would have opened, and she said the making was the whole of the winter. The ② drawer, meaning the box and not the signer, ran fourteen winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a drawer, she said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unopened.

Every ③ drawer in that house had the same short handle at the front of it, and the ④ drawer at the end, meaning the one they kept for the accounts and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A drawer, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to open; my grandmother said the opening is the part that fills fourteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the drawer was the whole of the story, meaning the signer and not the box. The ⑥ drawer, meaning the signer and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody pays and nobody sees; drawer, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a box and a signer. He said the signer is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ drawer had become a line in a design, and the design had become an argument about the short handle. The ⑧ drawer of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one house and fourteen winters of opening; drawer, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to open. She said the opening was never mentioned.

The ⑨ drawer I remember is the one numbered in the design, which stuck in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ drawer, my mother said in 1974, is the only one that improves by being opened; every drawer, she said, is a signer that has agreed to look like a box. She said the signer was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 抽屉（指那座房子里装着的那一格）
B. n. 抽屉（指那一格抽屉本身，与开票人相对）
C. 固定搭配：make a drawer 做一格抽屉
D. n. 抽屉（指留给账本用的那一格）
E. n. 抽屉（抽象总称，指一家人开抽屉的那些事）
F. n. 抽屉（指图样上写到、被标号的那一格）
G. n. 开票人；出票人（指故事里人人为之付钱却无人见过的那个人）
H. n. 开票人（抽象总称，指人人为之付钱却无人见过的那种人）

items.q: made a drawer that no child in the house would have opened
The drawer, meaning the box and not the signer
the drawer was the whole of the story
the drawer had become a line in a design
The drawer of the whole thing
A drawer, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: make a drawer 意为“做一格抽屉”，1951 年祖母做了一格屋子里没有一个孩子肯去打开的抽屉。
drawer 意为“抽屉”，指那一格抽屉本身而不是开票人，它经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
drawer 意为“抽屉”，指那座房子里的每一格抽屉，每一格正面都有同一个短短的把手。
drawer 意为“抽屉”，指留给账本用的那一格，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
drawer 意为“开票人、出票人”，指故事里人人为之付钱却无人见过的那个人，叔叔说这位开票人就是那个故事的全部。
drawer 意为“开票人”，指人人为之付钱却无人见过的那种人而不是那一格抽屉，是故事里人人为之付钱、却无人见过的东西。
drawer 意为“抽屉”，指图样上写到、被标号的那一格，到 1960 年这格抽屉成了图样里的一行。
drawer 意为“抽屉”，祖母一月写道，整件事开抽屉的那些事是一座房子和十四个冬天的开合。
drawer 意为“抽屉”，我记得的是图样上标号的那一格，1972 年卡住了，至今仍被说成屋子里最安静的一格。
drawer 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，一格抽屉是唯一会因为被好好打开而变得更好的东西。
